item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00388","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C20","C17"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.97,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C11 plausibly supplied a concrete delegation template: it designates an executive officer to perform statutory functions vested in the President \"without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President.\" The child closely reproduces that distinctive formulation while adapting it to department and agency heads, personnel, and newly enacted leave authority. C20 and C17 use substantially the same delegation machinery, but C11 is the strongest candidate because its language is nearly identical and it was issued only weeks before the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The heads of the several departments and agencies of the Government are hereby authorized and empowered, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, to exercise ... the authority conferred upon the President by section 202 (c) (2)","parent_excerpt":"The Director for Mutual Security is hereby designated and empowered to perform, without the approval, ratification, or other action of the President, the functions vested in the President by the Act of June 25, 1953","explanation":"Both provisions use the same distinctive delegation formula and connect it directly to authority statutorily vested in the President, with the child substituting different delegates and statutory functions."}]}
